task: AWS console: let the backup writer key reach the GFS prefixes, and turn on S3 Object Lock for the backup bucket

steps.human: Sign in to the AWS console with an admin login (not one of the backup IAM users). Press Done when the console home page shows.

steps.do: IAM > Users > the backup writer user (S3_BACKUP_BUCKET's write key) > Permissions: open its policy and read the JSON. Report the Resource list before changing anything.

Edit the policy JSON: keep the nightly/* resource and add <bucket>/monthly/*, <bucket>/quarterly/* and <bucket>/yearly/*. Add s3:PutObjectRetention and s3:PutObjectLegalHold to the write actions. Add a statement allowing s3:GetBucketObjectLockConfiguration on the bucket ARN. Save.

steps.human: Look over the saved policy. Press Done if it matches what Jax described in the chat.

steps.do: S3 > the backup bucket > Properties > Object Lock > Edit: enable Object Lock, default retention mode Compliance, 60 days. Fill the form but do not save.

steps.human: Compliance mode cannot be undone, and nobody (root included) can delete a locked object until its retention ends. Tick the acknowledgement and press Save changes yourself, then Done.

accept: On the next GFS boundary (1st of the month, 03:15-03:35 UTC), the dispatcher log has no 'GFS fanout upload ... failed' lines and the gfs-fanout heartbeat stays quiet. get-object-lock-configuration on the bucket returns Mode COMPLIANCE, Days 60.
notes: Sign-in pages are on signin.aws.amazon.com, which is deliberately not on the allow list: the extension lets go of the tab while the customer signs in.
Object Lock needs bucket versioning on, and it is checked before the form will save.
No save_secret step: nothing here creates a credential.
